what: profile2 feasibility: cost of candidate worlds F (foundry hidden weights) and G (gliders, hidden stress conversion) in the agent's box and the grading boxes; 2 x86 cloud cores of the cloud container
protocol: one mode per process (f_time.py, g_time.py; run_f.sh, run_g.sh), taskset -c 0,1, XLA_FLAGS='--xla_cpu_multi_thread_eigen=true intra_op_parallelism_threads=2', /home/user/evalwork/vecworld/vw1/.venv/bin/python (jax 0.12.0.1); compile timed apart (lower().compile()); timed calls repeated 3 times (median, [min, max]) unless n says otherwise; peak memory = ru_maxrss of the process (includes about 0.25 GB of imports)
mac: NOT MEASURED. The Mac's boxes are Linux aarch64 under Docker Desktop on Apple Silicon. No timing of this code on the Mac exists in the repository (rollouts so far ran in the cloud container). Inferred only: one Apple M-series performance core is usually 1.0 to 2.0 times one 2.1 GHz Xeon core on scalar code, and float64 SIMD is narrower on NEON (2 lanes) than AVX-512 (8 lanes, used by XLA here), so the ratio for these float64 kernels may be below 1. Running run_f.sh, run_g.sh and run_f32.sh once in a Mac box (about 45 min) replaces this guess with a factor.
